# Weekly Trader's Outlook

October 9, 2026  Rachel Dashiell

Major indexes reached record highs, but momentum divergences and defensive rotation suggest a more cautious backdrop. Oil prices and Treasury yields remain key variables.

## The Week That Was [...] My outlook for next week is "cautious." The primary considerations are: 1) Potential support beneath oil prices; 2) Negative momentum divergences in major indexes; 3) Improving trends in defensive sectors; and 4) Failed relative breakouts in Technology and High Beta.

Evidence that would challenge this view includes lower oil prices or yields, improving index momentum, renewed weakness in defensive sectors, and broader stock participation.

## Other Potential Market-Moving Catalysts [...] Last week, Nate maintained a "Moderately Bullish" outlook, citing a potential mean reversion in Treasury yields, pre-earnings season positioning, and favorable October seasonality. That view largely played out, with both the S&P 500 (SPX) and Nasdaq 100 (NDX) reaching new all-time highs.

If you read last Friday's blog, you might recall that I had a "breakout" outlook for stocks this week, noting that the S&P 500 Index (SPX) and Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) were at key intermediate-term support levels, which I felt set them up for an outsized weekly move (either higher or lower). There was a "bounce attempt" in stocks in the first half of this week (the Nasdaq was up 2% on the week by Wednesday's close) but then encountered a strong sell-off on Thursday, with some [...] 10-year yields decreased ~10 basis points (4.999% vs. 5.098%) while 30-year yields dropped ~12 basis points (5.318% vs. 5.437%). [...] April. Compared to last week, the SPX (white line) breadth moved up to 60.12% from 54.60%, the CCMP (blue line) fell to 36.61% from 36.59%, and the RUT (red line) dropped to 47.98% from 45.87%.

We are roughly two-thirds of the way through Q3 earnings season and overall, the results are thus far signaling strength. Out of the 301 S&P 500 companies that reported so far, 61% have beat on the top line and 82% have beat on the bottom line. Perhaps more importantly, the year-over-year revenue growth rate has been 13.64% and the earnings-per-share (EPS) growth rate is 29.37%.

## Outlook for Next Week [...] Friday (Nov. 6): Brookfield Asset Management (BAM), Enbridge Inc. (ENB), Humana Inc. (HUM), Moderna Inc. (MRNA), Plains All American Pipeline LP (PAA), PPL Corp. (PPL), Vistra Corp. (VST), Ubiquiti Inc. (UI) [...] forces is WTI Crude prices, which are up nearly 3% today and at a six-week high (last seen trading at $104.88/barrel).
